title: Treatment of Essential Occupiers in HDB Flats as Similar to Owners for Fulfillment of Minimum Occupation Period
what_it_is: Treatment of Essential Occupiers in HDB Flats as Similar to Owners for Fulfillment of Minimum Occupation Period

sections.label: Essential occupiers and HDB flats
sections.summary: Essential occupiers are part of the core family nucleus, must fulfil the MOP before buying private property, and cannot use CPF or housing grants for the flat.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: While essential occupiers are not flat owners, they form part of the core family nucleus that determines the household’s eligibility to own an HDB flat.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: HDB allows both of them to be listed as co-owners, or one of them as owner and the other as an essential occupier.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, essential occupiers are required to fulfil the MOP before they can purchase a private residential property.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, essential occupiers are not allowed to use their Central Provident Fund (CPF) or any housing grant received to pay for the flat.

sections.label: Essential occupiers and ABSD
sections.summary: As essential occupiers do not own the HDB flat, it is not in their property count, so they incur no ABSD on a first private property after MOP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As essential occupiers do not own their HDB flat, it is not included in their residential property count.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, they do not incur ABSD if they are Singapore Citizens buying their first private residential property after MOP.

sections.label: Spouses listed as occupiers
sections.summary: Only a small number list a spouse as an occupier, often for practical reasons with no intention to invest in private property after MOP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Only a small number list a spouse as an occupier, often for practical reasons with no intention to invest in a private residential property after fulfilling MOP.

sections.label: Hardship appeals to MND and HDB
sections.summary: Those with specific hardship can write in and appeal, and MND and HDB will consider on the merits, while the general policy principle remains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If there are instances of specific hardship, they can write in and appeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Ministry of National Development and HDB will consider on the merits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But the broad general policy principle which I have outlined does remain the principle underpinning the policy.
